A LITTLE CONTEXT

An encoding, not encryption.

Base64 represents bytes using printable characters. It is useful when binary data must travel through a text-only format. Anyone can decode it: Base64 does not keep secrets or replace encryption.

UTF-8 text → bytes → Base64

References: RFC 4648: Base encodings

Good to know

Will Chinese text and emoji work?

Yes. Encoding converts text to UTF-8 bytes before Base64. Decoding rejects bytes that are not valid UTF-8 instead of silently replacing them.

What is Base64URL?

Base64URL replaces + with − (the ASCII hyphen) and / with _. It often omits trailing = padding. Choose the URL-safe alphabet when processing Base64URL strings.

Why is decoding rejected?

Invalid characters, misplaced padding, impossible lengths or invalid trailing bits are rejected. A syntactically valid Base64 value can still contain binary data rather than UTF-8 text.

Can I decode a JWT here?

A whole JWT is not one Base64 value. Its segments use Base64URL. You can decode a segment here, but decoding does not verify its signature or authenticity.

PRACTICAL REFERENCE

Decode Base64 online: understand the result

Validate the alphabet and the output type before using decoded data. A successful decode does not establish that the content is safe or trustworthy.

Useful Base64 checks
Input or conditionWhat to expect
SGVsbG8=Decodes to Hello in UTF-8.
Zg (no padding)Decodes to f. Valid unpadded input is accepted.
_w== with URL-safe selectedValid Base64URL bytes, but not valid UTF-8 text. Text decoding is rejected.
Zh==Rejected: non-zero trailing bits are not canonical Base64.

Base64URL encode and decode

Choose URL-safe in the alphabet selector before encoding or decoding. Standard Base64 uses + and /; Base64URL uses the ASCII hyphen (-) and underscore (_). For the UTF-8 text 💡, standard Base64 is 8J+SoQ== and unpadded Base64URL is 8J-SoQ. Clear Include padding when encoding to generate the unpadded form.

Whitespace is ignored; a data URI prefix is not plain Base64 text. A JWT segment can be decoded as Base64URL, but decoding does not verify its signature.

Why “Base64 decrypt” is misleading

Decoding reverses an encoding, not encryption. There is no secret key. Do not use Base64 to protect passwords, tokens or confidential information.

Unicode, binary and image data

Text is encoded as UTF-8 before Base64. If decoded bytes are not valid UTF-8, this text tool reports an error. For image bytes or a data:image URI, use the dedicated image viewer.

What can safely be repaired?

This tool accepts valid missing padding, but does not guess damaged or truncated data. Check the original source rather than deleting arbitrary characters until a value decodes.
